approved_classes.ex:AminoAcid: A general class representing amino acids.
approved_classes.ex:EssentialAminoAcid: A specific type of amino acid that is essential for the body and must be obtained through food.
approved_classes.ex:SemiEssentialAminoAcid: A specific type of amino acid that can be produced in small amounts by the body but may need to be supplemented from food.
approved_classes.ex:NonEssentialAminoAcid: A specific type of amino acid that is not essential and can be synthesized by the body.
approved_classes.ex:NonPolarAminoAcid: A class representing non-polar (hydrophobic) amino acids that have no charge on the 'R' group.
approved_classes.ex:PolarAminoAcidNoChargeRGroup: A class representing polar amino acids with no charge on the 'R' group, which contribute to protein structure hydrogen bonding.
approved_classes.ex:PolarAminoAcidPositiveRGroup: A class representing polar amino acids with a positive 'R' group.
approved_classes.ex:PolarAminoAcidNegativeRGroup: A class representing polar amino acids with a negative 'R' group, which are aromatic dicarboxylic monoamino acids.
approved_classes.ex:Tyrosine: A specific type of amino acid that is involved in thyroid hormone production and has various other health benefits.
approved_classes.ex:D-Penicillamine: A non-standard amino acid used as a drug for chelation therapy, particularly in Wilson’s disease.
approved_classes.ex:N-Acetylcysteine: A non-standard amino acid used as an antioxidant and in the treatment of cystic fibrosis and chronic renal insufficiency.
approved_classes.ex:Gabapentin: A non-standard amino acid used as an anticonvulsant drug.

ex:hasCanonicalName.comment: Maps an amino acid to its canonical name.

ex:isEssential.comment: Indicates whether the amino acid is essential for the body.

ex:hasProperties.comment: Links an amino acid to its properties.

ex:isProducedByBody.comment: Indicates whether the amino acid is produced by the body or needs to be obtained through food.

ex:hasStructure.comment: Describes the structure of an amino acid.

ex:isDecarboxylatedTo.comment: Indicates the amino acid that results from decarboxylation of another amino acid.

ex:reactsWithAlcohol.comment: Indicates whether an amino acid can react with alcohol to form esters.

ex:reactsWithAmmonia.comment: Indicates whether an amino acid can react with ammonia to form amides.

ex:reactsWithMineralAcids.comment: Indicates whether an amino acid can react with mineral acids to form salts.

ex:reactsWithNinhydrin.comment: Indicates whether an amino acid reacts with ninhydrin to produce a color change.

ex:isSemiEssential.comment: Indicates whether the amino acid is semi-essential and requires supplementation from food.

ex:isNonPolar.comment: Indicates whether the amino acid is non-polar (hydrophobic) with no charge on the 'R' group.

ex:isPolarNoChargeRGroup.comment: Indicates whether the amino acid is polar with no charge on the 'R' group, contributing to protein structure hydrogen bonding.

ex:isPolarPositiveRGroup.comment: Indicates whether the amino acid is polar with a positive 'R' group.

ex:isPolarNegativeRGroup.comment: Indicates whether the amino acid is polar with a negative 'R' group, being aromatic dicarboxylic monoamino acids.

ex:treatsCondition.comment: Indicates the conditions that can be treated by a specific amino acid.

ex:isDrug.comment: Indicates whether an amino acid is used as a drug.
